column1: # consumers.tsv - who consumes a DLL -> engine call (issue 3303, epic 3300; design:
# research/05-graphics-composition/renderer-in-server-design.md section 2). Read by proxy/gen/classify.py into the last
# column `consumer` of policy-table.tsv and the `consumer` field of model.json's dll_to_engine methods.
#   exe       the EXE consumes it (it crosses); the default for every dll_to_engine row not listed here
#   renderer  only the server's renderer consumes it (it would stop crossing: a later epic's decision, written here)
#   both      the server's renderer takes it from the feed (server/src/feed/srv_feed.h) AND it crosses to the EXE
# One row per method: interface (the declaring interface, as policy-table.tsv names it), method, consumer, reason.
# Every row must name an existing dll_to_engine method; classify.py stops on an unknown method, a value outside the
# three above, an empty reason or a duplicate row. Lines starting with '#' are comments.

column4: reason
feed kPlotState: resource, improvement, route as the active team sees them (plot record layout fields); the EXE still draws improvements and routes in increment 2
feed kFeatureChanged: the plot record's feature; the EXE still draws features
feed kFowChanged: the plot record's fog bits; the EXE draws fog in increment 2
feed kCityCreated; the EXE draws cities
feed kCityDestroyed; the EXE draws cities
feed kCityCaptured; the EXE draws cities
feed kNaturalWonder (plot re-read at the next LeaveUpdate); the EXE shows the reveal
feed kWallCreated; the EXE draws city walls
feed kYieldChanged (plot re-read at the next LeaveUpdate); the EXE draws yield icons
feed kBorderChanged: the plot record's owner; the EXE draws borders in increment 2
feed kEraChanged (epic 0375): the player row's era, the seed allocator's era window; the EXE re-creates the units whose art changes
feed kUnitCreated (epic 0375): the unit table and the server's unit scene; the EXE keeps its Unit system (state ii-d)
feed kUnitMoved with its path (epic 0375): the unit table, the controller's move
feed kUnitTeleported (epic 0375): the unit's plot and facing
feed kUnitDestroyed (epic 0375): the record leaves the table, the seed allocator frees its index
feed kUnitDestroyedInCombat (epic 0375): the dead flag
feed kUnitSetDamage (epic 0375): the figure count
feed kUnitFortify (epic 0375): the fortified flag, the controller's fortify
feed kUnitWork (epic 0375): the controller's work action
feed kUnitParadrop (epic 0375): the controller's paradrop action
feed kUnitActivate (epic 0375): the controller's activate action
feed kUnitEmbark (epic 0375): the embarked flag; a creation when the key is unknown
feed kUnitGarrison (epic 0375): the garrisoned flag
feed kUnitShouldDimFlag (epic 0375): recorded only; the flag is the EXE's
feed kUnitVisibility (epic 0375): the visible flag and the fade
feed kUnitCombat with its combat record (epic 0375): the seed allocator's combat hold; the EXE's returned value goes back to the DLL
feed kCitySetDamage (epic 0375); the EXE draws cities
feed kCityPopulationChanged (epic 0375); the EXE draws cities
feed kCityCombat with its combat record (epic 0375): the seed allocator's combat hold; the EXE's returned value goes back to the DLL
feed kUnitMissionEnd (epic 0375): recorded; no event for the controller
feed kUnitRebased (epic 0375): the unit's plot
feed kUnitResetAnimationState (epic 0375): the controller's reset
